title: VEDA: Efficient LLM Generation Through Voting-based KV Cache Eviction and Dataflow-flexible Accelerator
problem: LLM inference on edge devices faces memory and computational bottlenecks due to intensive KV cache requirements and variable sequence lengths, limiting deployment feasibility.
motivation: Edge deployment demands efficient inference; KV cache memory pressure and varying sequence dimensions in generation phase create hardware complexity and latency.
method: Algorithm-hardware-dataflow tri-optimization: (1) voting-based KV cache eviction identifies unimportant kv vectors adaptively, reducing cache size while maintaining accuracy; (2) flexible-product dataflow with runtime-reconfigurable PE array handles diverse matrix-vector dimensions; (3) element-serial scheduling for nonlinear ops (softmax, layernorm). Hardware complexity reduced from O(N) to O(1). Custom VEDA accelerator implementation.
key_novelty: Adaptive KV cache voting for LLM inference combined with dataflow-flexible hardware for variable-dimension operations.
contributions: Voting-based KV cache eviction algorithm for adaptive importance filtering
Flexible-product dataflow with runtime-reconfigurable PE supporting variable dimensions
Element-serial scheduling for softmax/layernorm with O(1) hardware complexity
VEDA accelerator achieving superior latency/throughput on edge devices
limitations: Specific quantitative comparisons and device baselines not detailed in abstract; applicability to larger models unclear.
primary_theme: Adaptive KV cache and flexible dataflow for edge LLM inference
